Combine forecasts from mvgam models into a weighted ensemble

Source: R/ensemble.mvgam_forecast.R
ensemble.mvgam_forecast.Rd

Build a single mvgam_forecast from the hindcast and forecast draws of two or more mvgam_forecast objects. Each input supplies a share of the draws set by its weight. Weights are even by default.

Usage

ensemble(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_forecast'
ensemble(object, ..., weights = NULL, ndraws = 5000L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

object

An mvgam_forecast object returned by forecast.mvgam() or hindcast.mvgam().

...

More mvgam_forecast objects to combine.

weights

Either NULL (the default, equivalent to even weighting), or a numeric vector with one non-negative entry per supplied forecast. The weights are normalised to sum to 1. Strategies such as stacking need the fitted models. Compute them with loo_model_weights.mvgam() on the fits, or with loo_model_weights.mvgam_lfo() on their lfo_cv() results. Pass the numeric result here.

ndraws

Positive integer giving the total number of ensemble draws to return per series. Defaults to 5000. A model allocated more draws than it holds is sampled with replacement.

seed

Optional integer seed. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

Value

An object of class mvgam_forecast containing the ensembled hindcasts and forecasts. Suitable for plot.mvgam_forecast() and score.mvgam_forecast(). Attribute weights records the per-model weights used. Attribute ndraws_per_model records the integer draw counts drawn from each input.

Details

Per-model weights are split into integer draw counts that sum to ndraws by the largest-remainder rule, after brms::round_largest_remainder(). Each model then gives one set of sampled draws. Every series, in the hindcasts and in the forecasts, takes that same set. The ensemble keeps the dependence between series and the pairing of each hindcast with its forecast.

The returned object takes its series names, family, training data and test data from the first input. All inputs must share the series names, the hindcast lengths, the forecast horizons and, when present, the test observations.

A multivariate fit on a wide frame gives one forecast whose series are its responses. The ensemble is a forecast over those series. On a long frame the ensemble keeps one forecast per response. Every response takes the same draws.

See also

score.mvgam_forecast() scores the ensemble. loo_model_weights.mvgam_lfo() computes weights from forecast performance. pp_average.mvgam() averages predictions in place of forecasts. The forecast evaluation article weights an ensemble by leave-future-out stacking weights.

Other forecasting: compare_scores(), forecast.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), score.mvgam_forecast()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
# Two models of one count series: a smooth of x with and without
# an AR(1) trend
mod_gam <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), data = simdat$data_train,
                 family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 25 of 2000 (1.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
mod_ar <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
                data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
                chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
fc_gam <- forecast(mod_gam, newdata = simdat$data_test)
fc_ar <- forecast(mod_ar, newdata = simdat$data_test)

# An ensemble that draws 30% of its draws from the GAM
ens <- ensemble(fc_gam, fc_ar, weights = c(0.3, 0.7))
attr(ens, "ndraws_per_model")
#> fc_gam  fc_ar 
#>   1500   3500 
plot(ens)


# The ensemble scored against its components
scores <- compare_scores(fc_gam, fc_ar, ens, score = "drps",
                         model_names = c("GAM", "AR", "Ensemble"))
plot(scores, relative = "GAM")

# }
